title: Utilisation of Natural Resources in Crop and Livestock Farming

lessons.title: Assessing the farm's natural resources
lessons.html:
Know what the farm has

In this work experience module you take part in using and protecting the farm's natural resources: soil, water, veld, biodiversity and energy. Begin by assessing what the farm has, so that use can be planned within safe limits.

Resource assessment tasks

  • Soil: walk each land with your supervisor. Note soil colour, texture (sandy, loamy, clayey), slope, erosion signs and depth. Collect soil analysis reports and file them.
  • Water: list all sources: boreholes, dams, rivers, municipal or scheme water. Note how each is used, whether flows or levels are measured, and whether the use is registered or licensed under the National Water Act 36 of 1998.
  • Veld: describe the main grass and bush species in each camp, the condition of the veld and any bush encroachment. Note the recommended carrying capacity for the area.
  • Biodiversity: mark wetlands, riparian zones, indigenous bush and areas with invasive alien plants.
  • Energy: list diesel, electricity and solar use; note which pumps and machines use the most.

Making a resource map

On a farm map, mark lands, camps, water points, sensitive areas and problem areas such as dongas and alien plant stands. Use colours or symbols and a key. This map becomes the base for your planning and for showing progress over time.

Take dated photographs from fixed points so later visits can be compared. A photo of a donga today and the same view after repair is strong evidence for your portfolio.

Ask your supervisor to check and sign your assessment.

lessons.title: Using soil, water and veld wisely
lessons.html:
Practical resource management

Soil

  • Take part in soil sampling and help interpret results with your supervisor.
  • Apply lime and fertiliser as recommended, not by guesswork.
  • Use minimum tillage and keep residues on the surface where the system allows.
  • Help maintain contour banks and waterways; report new erosion.

Water

  • Read water meters or measure dam levels and record them weekly.
  • Check troughs, pipes and irrigation systems for leaks and fix or report them.
  • Help schedule irrigation using soil moisture readings or weather data.
  • Keep livestock out of sensitive river banks by using troughs and fencing.
  • Never wash spray equipment or dispose of chemicals near water.

Veld

  • Follow the grazing plan: move animals on the planned dates and record grazing days per camp.
  • Assess grass cover before and after grazing.
  • Help with bush control and alien plant clearing using approved methods and correct PPE.
  • Take part in fire management only under supervision: firebreaks must be prepared, the burn must follow a plan and local fire protection association rules, and firefighting equipment and people must be ready.

The Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 requires land users to protect these resources and control declared weeds and invaders. Your records show that the farm is meeting this duty.

Write each task in your logbook with the date, what you did, the resource involved and the result, and ask your supervisor to sign it. Include photos where they help show the work done.

Discuss any problems you find with your supervisor the same day.

lessons.title: Recording, reporting and improving resource use
lessons.html:
Evidence and continuous improvement

Records to keep

ResourceRecord
SoilSoil analysis results, lime and fertiliser applied per land
WaterMeter readings, irrigation applied, rainfall
VeldGrazing days, stock numbers per camp, photo points
BiodiversityArea cleared of alien plants, wetland condition
EnergyDiesel and electricity use per month

Analysing your records

Calculate simple indicators. For example, if 600 mm of irrigation was applied to a land producing 12 t/ha of maize, compare this with another land that used 750 mm for the same yield. The first land uses water more efficiently; find out why, perhaps a better soil, better scheduling or fewer leaks.

Reporting

Write a short monthly report for your supervisor: what was done, problems found, readings, and recommendations. Use plain language, dates and numbers. Report urgent issues at once, such as a burst pipe, a pollution incident or a veld fire.

Improvement project

Choose one resource problem on the farm, such as a leaking dam wall, an eroding road or a stand of invasive wattle, and plan a small project to address it. Include the cause, proposed action, labour and cost, and how you will measure success. Carry out the project if your supervisor approves, and record before and after evidence.

Key points

  • Start with a resource assessment and a map of the farm.
  • Use fixed photo points to show changes over time.
  • Record water readings, grazing days, fertiliser and energy use.
  • Fire management only under supervision, with firebreaks and a plan.
  • Use records to find and fix inefficient resource use.

quiz.question: Why should photographs be taken from fixed points?

options.text: They look better in a report
So later photos can be compared to show change
It is required for every photo on a farm

quiz.question: Which Act requires land users to protect soil and veld and control declared weeds?

options.text: Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983

quiz.question: Two lands both yield 12 t/ha. One used 600 mm of irrigation and the other 750 mm. Which is more water-efficient?
How often should water meters or dam levels be recorded in this module?

options.text: Only when there is a drought

quiz.question: What must be in place before a planned veld burn?

options.text: Prepared firebreaks, a burning plan and firefighting equipment and people
A windy day to spread the fire

quiz.question: Spray equipment may be washed in the farm dam if it is rinsed well afterwards.
A burst pipe or pollution incident should be reported immediately.
Which should be listed when assessing water resources? (select all that apply)

options.text: All water sources, such as boreholes and dams
Whether the use is registered or licensed
The colour of the water tank
